```{r setup, include = FALSE}
options(width = 80L, covr.record_tests = TRUE)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(

library("tools")
```

# Context


```{r loading}
pkg <- params$package
pkg_name <- params$package_name
pkg_version <- params$package_version
risk_path <- params$assessment_path
image <- params$image
val_date <- params$val_date
val_dir <- params$val_dir
repo_url <- params$repo_url

d_riskmetric <- readRDS(risk_path)

# Required fields
required_fields <- c("r_cmd_check", "license", "remote_checks", "covr_coverage")

# Missing fields
missing_fields <- setdiff(required_fields, names(d_riskmetric))

# Assign default error structure for missing fields to avoid errors
for (field in missing_fields) {
  d_riskmetric[[field]] <- structure(NA, class = c("pkg_metric_error", "pkg_metric"))
}
```

```{r context, results='asis'}
cat("This report was generated by the `val.pipeline` package as part of a",
    "package validation run.\n\n", sep = " ")

cat("> - **Validation date (`val_date`):** ",
    if (!is.null(val_date) && nzchar(val_date)) val_date else "unknown",
    "\n", sep = "")
cat("> - **Validation directory (`val_dir`):** ",
    if (!is.null(val_dir) && nzchar(val_dir)) val_dir else "unknown",
    "\n", sep = "")
cat("> - **Origin (`source`):** ",
    riskreports:::get_pkg_origin(params$source),
    "\n", sep = "")
# Source repo URL. This is the actual URL the package tarball was
# pulled from during the run (e.g. a date-pinned PPM snapshot). Its
# basename is the snapshot repo name in Posit Package Manager, so
# reviewers can trace a rendered report back to a specific PPM
# snapshot without cross-referencing `qual_metadata.rds`. (#114)
if (!is.null(repo_url) && length(repo_url) == 1L && nzchar(repo_url)) {
  cat("> - **Source repo URL (`repo_url`):** ", repo_url, "\n", sep = "")
}
```


# Package Assessments

## Metric-based risk assessment

The following metrics are derived from the `riskmetric` R package.

```{r create_r_riskmetric, warning=FALSE}
# Assesment produces a data.frame with one row
r_riskmetric <- riskreports::assessment(d_riskmetric)
is_na <- sapply(r_riskmetric, function(x) {
  is.na(x) || (is.character(x) && startsWith(x, "no applicable"))
})
r_riskmetric$origin <- riskreports:::get_pkg_origin(params$source)
```


::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}

```{r info_cards}
riskreports:::create_metrics_cards(r_riskmetric)
```

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="html"}

```{r simple_cards, include=FALSE}
# The Downloads 1yr / Reverse dependencies / License / Origin fields
# that used to render as a separate summary-card table for non-HTML
# outputs have been folded into the main metric table below.
# Origin is now displayed as a bullet in the Context section, so this
# chunk only clears the placeholder `$origin` column added upstream
# (which is used by the HTML info-cards path) before `summary_table()`
# renders the metric table.
r_riskmetric$origin <- NULL
```

:::

```{r prepare_tables_namespace}
# Some assessments store exported-namespace names with literal surrounding
# quote characters (e.g. cli's `"__cli_update_due"` is 18 bytes long — 16
# for the name plus two `"` bytes). Left as-is, subsetting `export_help`
# by `exported_namespace` returns NA-named entries, which downstream
# triggers `data.frame(... check.names = FALSE): row names contain
# missing values` inside `prepare_namespace_table()`. Strip stray quotes
# from both metrics so the two vectors align.
if (!is.null(d_riskmetric$export_help) &&
    !is.null(names(d_riskmetric$export_help))) {
  names(d_riskmetric$export_help) <- gsub('^"|"$', "",
                                          names(d_riskmetric$export_help))
}
if (!is.null(d_riskmetric$exported_namespace) &&
    is.character(d_riskmetric$exported_namespace)) {
  d_riskmetric$exported_namespace <- gsub('^"|"$', "",
                                          d_riskmetric$exported_namespace)
}
namespace_table <- tryCatch(
  riskreports:::prepare_namespace_table(d_riskmetric),
  error = function(e) {
    htmltools::span(paste0("Exported-namespace table unavailable: ",
                           conditionMessage(e)))
  }
)
```

```{r prepare_tables_dependencies}
deps <- d_riskmetric$dependencies
deps$package <- gsub("\\n", " ", deps$package)
# row.names(deps) <- NULL
dependencies_table <- htmltools::div(
  htmltools::span(

)
```

```{r prepare_tables_reverse_dependencies}
reverse_dependencies <- if (inherits(rdep_raw, "pkg_metric_error") ||

} else {
```

```{r prepare_tables_news}
news_content <- paste0(
  "The package has ",
  if ("has_news" %in% names(d_riskmetric) && !is.null(d_riskmetric$has_news)) d_riskmetric$has_news,
  " NEWS file and it is ",
```

```{r general-riskmetric, warning=FALSE}
#| tab.cap: "**Package general assessment:** Coverage, check results, size, 
#|  download the last year, reverse dependencies and number of dependencies."

# Defensively drop columns whose value is NULL, empty, or entirely NA
# before handing r_riskmetric to summary_table(). This prevents downstream
# data.frame() calls (some of which use check.names = FALSE) from failing
# with "row names contain missing values" when a metric column is an error
# object, a list, or a multi-element vector whose NA-check would recycle.
.keep_cols <- vapply(r_riskmetric, function(x) {
  if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0) return(FALSE)
  suppressWarnings(!all(is.na(x)))
}, logical(1))
summary_data <- summary_table(r_riskmetric[, .keep_cols, drop = FALSE]) |>
  stats::setNames(c("Metric", "Value"))
row.names(summary_data) <- NULL

# The `summary_table()` helper runs every numeric metric through
# `is_logical()`, which coerces a value of exactly `1` to the string
# `"Yes"`. That reads correctly for boolean flags (has_news, etc.) but
# is misleading for count metrics like `dependencies` and
# `reverse_dependencies` when a package happens to have exactly one.
# Restore the raw counts for those two rows so the reader sees a number.
.restore_count <- function(metric_row_name, count_value) {
  if (is.null(count_value) || length(count_value) == 0) return(invisible())
  n <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(count_value[[1]]))
  if (is.na(n)) return(invisible())
  idx <- which(summary_data$Metric == metric_row_name)
  if (length(idx) == 1L) {
    summary_data$Value[idx] <<- prettyNum(n, big.mark = ",")
  }
}
.restore_count("Dependencies",
               if (inherits(d_riskmetric$dependencies, "data.frame"))
                 nrow(d_riskmetric$dependencies) else
                 length(d_riskmetric$dependencies))
.restore_count("Reverse dependencies",
               if (is.character(d_riskmetric$reverse_dependencies))
                 length(d_riskmetric$reverse_dependencies) else
                 d_riskmetric$reverse_dependencies)
.restore_count("Has vignettes",
               if (is.numeric(d_riskmetric$has_vignettes))
                 d_riskmetric$has_vignettes else NULL)

# --- Extra polish on individual summary rows -----------------------------
.set_value <- function(metric_row_name, val) {
  if (is.null(val) || !length(val) || !nzchar(as.character(val))) {
    return(invisible())
  }
  idx <- which(summary_data$Metric == metric_row_name)
  if (length(idx) == 1L) summary_data$Value[idx] <<- as.character(val)
}

# Export help: show "N / M (P%)" derived from the raw per-export logical.
.eh <- d_riskmetric$export_help
if (is.logical(.eh) && length(.eh) > 0) {
  .n <- sum(.eh, na.rm = TRUE)
  .m <- length(.eh)
  .set_value("Export help",
             sprintf("%s / %s (%.1f%%)",
                     prettyNum(.n, big.mark = ","),
                     prettyNum(.m, big.mark = ","),
                     100 * .n / .m))
}

# Bugs status: round the percent-closed figure to one decimal place.
.bs <- d_riskmetric$bugs_status
if (is.logical(.bs) && length(.bs) > 0) {
  .set_value("Bugs status",
             sprintf("%.1f%% closed", 100 * sum(.bs, na.rm = TRUE) / length(.bs)))
}

# Size codebase: pretty-print with a thousands separator.
.sc <- d_riskmetric$size_codebase
if (is.numeric(.sc) && length(.sc) >= 1) {
  .set_value("Size codebase",
             prettyNum(as.integer(.sc[[1]]), big.mark = ","))
}

# Websites: show the associated URL(s) rather than a boolean "Yes".
.ws <- d_riskmetric$has_website
if (is.character(.ws) && length(.ws) > 0) {
  .ws <- .ws[nzchar(.ws) & !is.na(.ws)]
  if (length(.ws) > 0) {
    .set_value("Has website", paste(.ws, collapse = ", "))
  }
}

# Bug reports URL: the `has_bug_reports_url` metric only records presence
# (0/1), not the URL itself. Try to extract the URL from the package's
# sourced DESCRIPTION file when the run's val_dir is available.
if (!is.null(val_dir) && nzchar(as.character(val_dir))) {
  .desc_path <- file.path(as.character(val_dir), "sourced",
                          as.character(pkg_name), "DESCRIPTION")
  if (file.exists(.desc_path)) {
    .desc <- tryCatch(read.dcf(.desc_path), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(.desc)) {
      .br <- if ("BugReports" %in% colnames(.desc)) .desc[1, "BugReports"] else NA
      if (!is.na(.br) && nzchar(.br)) {
        .set_value("Has bug reports url", as.character(.br))
      }
      # Has source control fallback. `pkg_metric_has_source_control()`
      # in {riskmetric} returns "unknown" when it can't parse a code
      # host URL from the pkg's URL field, but the URL is often
      # present in `DESCRIPTION` -- just as a plain github.com /
      # gitlab.com / bitbucket.org link that riskmetric didn't
      # recognize. Extract it here rather than showing "unknown".
      # See #130.
      .url <- if ("URL" %in% colnames(.desc)) .desc[1, "URL"] else NA
      if (!is.na(.url) && nzchar(.url)) {
        .url_bits <- trimws(unlist(strsplit(as.character(.url),
                                            "[,\\s]+")))
        .url_bits <- .url_bits[nzchar(.url_bits)]
        .code_hosts <- c("github.com", "gitlab.com", "bitbucket.org",
                         "codeberg.org", "sr.ht", "gitea.io")
        .src_urls <- .url_bits[
          vapply(.url_bits,
                 function(u) any(vapply(.code_hosts,
                                        function(h) grepl(h, u, fixed = TRUE),
                                        logical(1))),
                 logical(1))
        ]
        if (length(.src_urls) > 0L) {
          .set_value("Has source control",
                     paste(unique(.src_urls), collapse = ", "))
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

# --- Append rows folded in from the former "Simple cards" + "Code checks"
# sections: Downloads 1yr, Reverse dependencies, License, R CMD check, and
# Remote checks. Each is added only when the underlying metric is available.
.append_row <- function(metric_row_name, val) {
  if (is.null(val) || !length(val)) return(invisible())
  val_chr <- as.character(val)
  if (!nzchar(val_chr) || is.na(val_chr)) return(invisible())
  if (metric_row_name %in% summary_data$Metric) {
    .set_value(metric_row_name, val_chr)
    return(invisible())
  }
  summary_data <<- rbind(
    summary_data,
    data.frame(Metric = metric_row_name, Value = val_chr,
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
  )
}

# Downloads 1yr
.dl <- r_riskmetric$downloads_1yr
if (is.numeric(.dl) && length(.dl) >= 1 && !is.na(.dl[[1]])) {
  .append_row("Downloads 1yr", prettyNum(as.integer(.dl[[1]]), big.mark = ","))
}

# Reverse dependencies — pull the raw character vector from d_riskmetric
# (r_riskmetric$reverse_dependencies has already been reduced to a count).
.rd_raw <- d_riskmetric$reverse_dependencies
if (is.character(.rd_raw) && length(.rd_raw) > 0) {
  .append_row("Reverse dependencies",
              prettyNum(length(.rd_raw), big.mark = ","))
} else if (is.numeric(.rd_raw) && length(.rd_raw) >= 1 && !is.na(.rd_raw[[1]])) {
  .append_row("Reverse dependencies",
              prettyNum(as.integer(.rd_raw[[1]]), big.mark = ","))
}

# License
.lic <- r_riskmetric$license
if (!is.null(.lic) && length(.lic) >= 1 && nzchar(as.character(.lic[[1]]))) {
  .append_row("License", as.character(.lic[[1]]))
}

# R CMD check — format the named-count breakdown (Notes / Errors / Warnings)
# on one line so it sits cleanly in a table cell.
.rc <- d_riskmetric[["r_cmd_check"]]
if (!riskreports::is_risk_error(.rc) && !is.null(names(.rc))) {
  .append_row(
    "R CMD check",
    paste(stringr::str_to_title(names(.rc)), .rc, sep = " - ",
          collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Remote checks — scalar string when available.
.rmt <- d_riskmetric[["remote_checks"]]
if (!riskreports::is_risk_error(.rmt) && length(.rmt) >= 1) {
  .append_row("Remote checks", as.character(.rmt[[1]]))
}

# Code coverage — pull the same scalar the standalone Code coverage
# section used to compute (percent for numeric metrics, raw text
# otherwise) and expose it as a metric-table row. When the metric
# is unavailable, still render the row with "Not calculated" so the
# reader knows coverage was considered.
.cov <- d_riskmetric[["covr_coverage"]]
.cov_scalar <- if (is.list(.cov)) {
  if (!is.null(.cov$totalcoverage)) .cov$totalcoverage else .cov[[1]]
} else {
  .cov
}
.cov_display <- if (!riskreports::is_risk_error(.cov) &&
                    !is.null(.cov_scalar) && length(.cov_scalar) == 1 &&
                    !is.na(.cov_scalar) &&
                    (is.numeric(.cov_scalar) || is.character(.cov_scalar))) {
  if (is.numeric(.cov_scalar)) sprintf("%.2f%%", .cov_scalar)
  else as.character(.cov_scalar)
} else {
  "Not calculated"
}
.append_row("Code coverage", .cov_display)

# Reorder rows into a friendlier grouping:
#   1. Downloads 1yr + Reverse dependencies (top)
#   2. Dependencies
#   3. R CMD check + Code coverage + Remote checks (paired trio)
#   4. Has news + News current (paired)
#   5. Exported namespace + Export help (paired)
#   6. Has examples + Has vignettes (paired)
#   7. URL-returning fields: Has website, Has source control, Has bug
#      reports url, followed immediately by Bugs status.
#   8. Everything else (e.g. Size codebase) keeps its original relative
#      order after the groups above.
#   9. License + Has maintainer (bottom)
.preferred_order <- c(
  "Downloads 1yr", "Reverse dependencies",
  "Dependencies",
  "R CMD check", "Code coverage", "Remote checks",
  "Has news", "News current",
  "Exported namespace", "Export help",
  "Has examples", "Has vignettes",
  "Has website", "Has source control", "Has bug reports url", "Bugs status"
)
.bottom_pinned <- c("License", "Has maintainer")
.metric_order  <- summary_data$Metric
.head_rows     <- intersect(.preferred_order, .metric_order)
.tail_rows     <- intersect(.bottom_pinned, .metric_order)
.middle_rows   <- setdiff(.metric_order, c(.head_rows, .tail_rows))
.new_order     <- c(.head_rows, .middle_rows, .tail_rows)
summary_data   <- summary_data[match(.new_order, summary_data$Metric), , drop = FALSE]
row.names(summary_data) <- NULL

values_collapsed_rows <- c(
  "Has news",
  "Exported namespace",
  "Dependencies",
  "Reverse dependencies",
  "Has examples"
)

indexes_collapsed_rows <- which(summary_data$Section %in% values_collapsed_rows)

is_html <- knitr::is_html_output(excludes = "markdown")

# Certain rows of this table are collapsible, containing detailed information.
if (isTRUE(is_html)) {
  reactable::reactable(
  summary_data,
  rownames = FALSE,
  pagination = FALSE,
  details = function(index) {
    if(index %in% indexes_collapsed_rows) {
      collapsed_content <- switch(summary_data$Section[index],
        "Exported namespace" = namespace_table,
        "Dependencies" =  dependencies_table,
        "Reverse dependencies" = reverse_dependencies,
        "Has examples" = examples_content,
        "Has news" = news_content
      )
      htmltools::div(
        style = "padding: 1rem;",
        collapsed_content
      )
    }
  },
  columns = list(
    Section = reactable::colDef(
      name = ""
    ),
    Values = reactable::colDef(
      name = "",
      cell = function(value) {
        if (value ==  "Yes") {
          # Green 'Yes'
          htmltools::span(value, style = "color:var(--bs-success); font-weight: bold;")
        } else if (value == "No") {
          # Red 'No'
          htmltools::span(value, style = "color: var(--bs-danger); font-weight: bold;")
        } else {
          htmltools::span(value, style = "color: var(--bs-body-color); font-weight: bold;")
        }
      },
      align = "center"
    )
  ),
  class = "metrics-table"
)
} else {
  knitr::kable(summary_data)
}
```

```{r dependencies_section_prep, include=FALSE}
.deps_raw <- d_riskmetric$dependencies
.deps_df <- NULL
.deps_names <- character(0)
if (inherits(.deps_raw, "data.frame") && "package" %in% names(.deps_raw)) {
  .deps_df <- as.data.frame(.deps_raw, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  .deps_df <- .deps_df[, intersect(c("package", "type"), names(.deps_df)), drop = FALSE]
  .deps_df$package <- as.character(.deps_df$package)
  if ("type" %in% names(.deps_df)) {
    .deps_df$type <- as.character(.deps_df$type)
  } else {
    .deps_df$type <- NA_character_
  }
  .deps_df <- .deps_df[nzchar(.deps_df$package) & !is.na(.deps_df$package), , drop = FALSE]
  # Prefer a friendly ordering: Depends, Imports, LinkingTo, Suggests, Enhances,
  # then any other type, then alphabetical within each type.
  .type_rank <- c("Depends" = 1L, "Imports" = 2L, "LinkingTo" = 3L,
                  "Suggests" = 4L, "Enhances" = 5L)
  .deps_df$.rank <- unname(ifelse(.deps_df$type %in% names(.type_rank),
                                  .type_rank[.deps_df$type], 99L))
  .deps_df <- .deps_df[order(.deps_df$.rank, .deps_df$type, .deps_df$package), , drop = FALSE]
  .deps_df$.rank <- NULL
  rownames(.deps_df) <- NULL
  .deps_names <- .deps_df$package
} else if (is.character(.deps_raw)) {
  .deps_names <- as.character(.deps_raw)
  .deps_names <- .deps_names[nzchar(.deps_names) & !is.na(.deps_names)]
  .deps_names <- sort(unique(.deps_names))
  .deps_df <- if (length(.deps_names) > 0) {
    data.frame(
      package = .deps_names,
      type = NA_character_,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
      row.names = NULL
    )
  } else {
    data.frame(
      package = character(0),
      type = character(0),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
      row.names = NULL
    )
  }
}
.has_deps <- length(.deps_names) > 0

.rdep_raw <- d_riskmetric$reverse_dependencies
.rdep_names <- character(0)
if (!inherits(.rdep_raw, "pkg_metric_error") && is.character(.rdep_raw)) {
  .rdep_names <- as.character(.rdep_raw)
}
.rdep_names <- .rdep_names[nzchar(.rdep_names) & !is.na(.rdep_names)]
.rdep_names <- sort(unique(.rdep_names))
.has_rdeps <- length(.rdep_names) > 0
```

```{r dependencies_section, eval=.has_deps, results='asis'}
cat("## Dependencies", "\n\n")
cat(sprintf("This package has %s first-order dependenc%s:\n\n",
            prettyNum(length(.deps_names), big.mark = ","),
            if (length(.deps_names) == 1L) "y" else "ies"))
.deps_show <- .deps_df
names(.deps_show) <- c("Package", "Type")[seq_len(ncol(.deps_show))]
if ("Type" %in% names(.deps_show)) {
  .deps_show$Type[is.na(.deps_show$Type) | !nzchar(.deps_show$Type)] <- "—"
}
print(knitr::kable(.deps_show, row.names = FALSE))
cat("\n\n")
```

# Installation environment


## System Info

```{r execution_info}
#| tab.cap: "**System information**. Table about the system used to check the package."
tt_sys_info_df <- data.frame(
  Field = c("OS", "Platform", "System", "Execution Time"),
  Value = c(
    sessionInfo()$running,
    R.version$platform,
    R.version$system,
    format(Sys.time(), tz = "UTC", usetz = TRUE)
  ))

knitr::kable(tt_sys_info_df)
```

<!--
From here we use the lua filter based on this issue from Quarto itself
https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/341
Please take into account that not all content in the chunks will be correctly folded
- character vectors are
- reactable tables are not
An alternative is to use callout blocks with collapse = TRUE
The advantage of the foldable_code lua filter is that the code is printed exactly as in the R console
-->

## Information about the environment
Environmental and options variables affect how package checks and software in it might behave.

```{r computing, attr.output='.details summary="Environmental variables when running this report"'}
riskreports::environ_report(exclude = c("GITHUB_PAT", "APPDATA", 
                                        "GITHUB", "GITLAB_PAT", "GITLAB",
                                        "ProgramFiles", "ProgramFiles(x86)",
                                        "R_USER", "USERNAME", "USERPROFILE", 
                                        "USERDNSDOMAIN", "USERDOMAIN", 
                                        "USERDOMAIN_ROAMINGPROFILE", "R_DptShare"              
                                        ))
```

```{r options, attr.output='.details summary="These are the options set to generate the report"'}
riskreports::options_report(exclude = c("usethis.full_name", "usethis.description", "usethis.destdir"))
```
